classification.difficultyReason: Relate an angle of depression to the angle at the ship and apply tangent.

content.prompt: The angle of depression from a point $A$ to a ship at point $B$ is $10^\circ$. If the distance $BX$ from $B$ to the foot of the cliff at $X$ is $800\text{ m}$, find the height of the cliff, correct to the nearest metre.

spec.sourceRegion: Review exercise question 9, right-hand cliff figure
spec.description: A vertical cliff AX with a narrow hatched cliff body to its left, horizontal ground extending through B, and a red dashed line of sight AB. No angle arc or horizontal reference through A is supplied.
spec.mathematics: AX is vertical, XB horizontal, A above X and B to the right of X. XB is 800 m; the angle of depression is given only in the question text.
spec.answerVisibility: Only source givens are visible; the cliff height and derived angle at B are not supplied.

answer.worked:
The angle of elevation at $B$ equals the angle of depression, so $\angle ABX=10^\circ$ (alternate angles between horizontal lines). Let the cliff height be $h$ metres.
$$\begin{align*}\tan10^\circ&=\frac{h}{800}\\h&=800\tan10^\circ\\h&\approx141\text{ m}.\end{align*}$$
